Borrower, saver and portfolio figures come from different sources and definitions and do not yet form one trend

Report an error

01What does this evidence establish?

Among providers reporting to the Social Fund for Development (SFD), verified primary tables record 93,118 active borrowers at end-2015 and 88,445 at end-2020. A 2024 policy paper citing SFD/SMED data reports 78,686 at end-2023; the set of providers it covers has not been verified. The same paper reports what it calls 3.3 million “active savers” at microfinance banks in 2023 and a nominal portfolio of about YER44 billion; the verified 2020 anchors are 1,611,206 savers/depositors and YER33.379 billion. “Active savers” and “savers/depositors” have not been shown to be the same measure, and both portfolio figures are nominal rials: between December 2020 and December 2023 the average market rate published by the Central Bank of Yemen – Aden (CBY-Aden) moved from about 793 to about 1,529 rials per US dollar, and the evidence base does not record which rial valuation, across Yemen's divided monetary areas, the portfolio figures use, so no real or US-dollar change can be derived from them. Because the 2023 primary source document, the exact set of providers covered, saver definition/deduplication and period bridge are not yet available in the evidence base for direct verification, these are separate reference points, each with stated limits, not a trend. Together they do not establish unique people, real credit growth, broader inclusion, improved borrower outcomes or causality.

02What does it measure?

Active microfinance borrowers at end-2015, end-2020 and end-2023, and savers or depositors and nominal loan portfolio at end-2020 and in 2023, from providers reporting to the Social Fund for Development (SFD) for 2015 and 2020 and from a 2024 policy paper citing SFD/SMED data for 2023, set side by side as separate figures rather than one series.

03Who or what does it apply to?

Microfinance borrower, saver/depositor and nominal-portfolio measures drawn from provider and reporting groups defined by each source, which are not yet fully harmonized across years.

04How current is it?

The latest figure in this comparison refers to the end of 2023 and comes from a secondary source; it does not describe the market in 2026. The comparison is reassessed if the 2023 primary source and the set of providers it covers become available for direct verification, or if a newer comparable primary observation is added.

05What this evidence does not establish

The figures do not show broader inclusion, real credit deepening, a harmonized trend, improved borrower outcomes, a causal effect, growth in unique people or an unchanged set of providers.

07Method and verification detail

Detail for reproducing or challenging this record without changing what it means.

How was it produced?

Figures taken as published from the year-end provider tables of the Social Fund for Development (SFD) for 2015 and 2020 and from the 2024 policy paper for 2023, with the December 2020 and December 2023 average market exchange rates published by the Central Bank of Yemen – Aden (CBY-Aden) shown for context. No trend, growth rate, or real or US-dollar value is calculated, because the provider set, the saver definition and the link between periods are unresolved.

When does this record change?

This record is updated when an authoritative source is revised or replaced, a newer comparable observation becomes available, the definition, population or method changes, or the conditions for public use change.

How can I verify it?

This record is drawn from the source(s) listed on this page. Open a source record to reach the original document, and check that the definition, period, population and geography match what is stated here.

How should this record be read?

Read this evidence within the definition, population or group covered, calculation base where relevant, period, geography and method shown on the page. Before reusing or comparing it, check the source, limitations, evidence date and correction history. If a value or source link is unavailable, the page says so rather than filling the gap by inference. This resource does not host source files; where an original-source link is given, check the publisher’s terms before republishing.
